messages:
jun: seeing odd outbound calls from preview-renderer -> 169.254.169.254 during support embed rendering. captured request/response. possible SSRF to metadata service.
mika: can you paste the repro?
jun: repro curl: 
```
curl -v "https://staging.redwood.ai/support/embed?url=http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/instance-id" -H "Authorization: Bearer $SUPPORT_TOKEN"
```
response body contained `i-0abcd1234` (internal instance id).
sec-oncall: marking P0 (server-side SSRF to metadata). immediate containment: block renderer egress to link-local and internal CIDRs, disable external fetch in support embed feature flag.
sre-bot: egress ACL update started -> denied 169.254.0.0/16, 10.0.0.0/8 from preview-renderer cluster id=prndr-3. rule apply in progress.
eng-sre: flipping feature flag support.embed.external_fetch=false in prod configstore.
frontend: pushed quick change to return 400 if url host matches internal IPs. PR #5021.
deploy-bot: configstore change applied; feature flag propagation success.
jun: good — staging reproducer fails after flag off. need to rotate renderer service credentials used by CI and support bots.
sec-oncall: agree. rotate service tokens and revoke any short-lived creds that allowed fetches. add rotation job.
eng-sre: started key rotation for renderer service keys. rotated key id=srk-77 -> new key srk-78; revoked old tokens.
auditsvc-bot: creating signed audit record: event=ssrf-detection actor=jun env=staging signed=true key=kms://global/keyRings/audit/cryptoKeys/signing-key
frontend: note: root cause — preview renderer trusted unvalidated url param and allowed fetches from arbitrary hosts. also returned raw body into iframe srcdoc. combined SSRF+potential data leak.
mika: can we confirm prod was hit? logs query for last 30d for requests to metadata IP from renderer service.
eng-sre: running query... found 2 outbound calls from renderer-prod last 48h from support-account-112. timestamps attached. digging session IDs now.
product-security: any evidence of customer data exfil? what was fetched besides instance-id?
jun: looked at captured responses: mostly internal metadata endpoints; no S3 presigned URLs or DB credentials seen. no anomalous downstream requests from those sessions.
sec-oncall: set incident severity P2 for now (no confirmed customer data exfil). containment done. next actions: 1) enforce host allowlist on renderer, 2) add server-side SSRF sanitizer, 3) sign audit logs with KMS and persist to immutable bucket, 4) rotate keys (in progress), 5) run retroactive scan of logs for suspicious fetches, 6) RBAC change: only support-admin role allowed to render external embeds, 7) schedule postmortem.
frontend: implementing strict allowlist and forcing fetch through proxy that strips auth headers. PR #5024 open.
eng-sre: will forward audit records to s3://redwood-audit-prod/ssrf-incidents/ and enable object-lock for 90d retention. using kms://projects/redwood/locations/global/keyRings/audit/cryptoKeys/obj-lock-key for SSE-KMS.
auditsvc-bot: audit record signed and forwarded -> s3://redwood-audit-prod/ssrf-1787654321.json signed=true
deploy-bot: canary deploy for renderer-service sha=9b1cde started
deploy-bot: canary success, promoting to prod in 10% -> 50% -> 100% steps
mika: regression tests added: SSRF fuzzing harness + CI check that disallows fetching link-local addresses.
product-security: drafting internal customer impact assessment. so far, no customer-facing data accessed — will prepare template if escalation needed.
compliance: preserve all logs, audit records, and rotated keys metadata for 180 days. tagging incident INC-20260325-ssrf.
sec-oncall: assign postmortem owner and schedule 60m blameless review in 24h. owner=mika. add timeline, root cause, detection lead, containment actions, and remediation tasks.
jun: adding notes and evidence to the incident doc. leaving reproduction steps and proof-of-fix.
sec-oncall: closing triage loop. keep channel updated if any new findings. thanks all. :lock:
